dedupe_keys.name: aotearoa new zealand economic benefits of space weather mitigation investment for the transmission grid

description: This case study assesses the economic benefits of investing in space weather mitigation for Aotearoa New Zealand's electricity transmission network. Edward Oughton, Andrew Renton, Daniel Mac Marnus, Dennies Bor and Craig Rodger posted it on arXiv in July 2025 (version 3 in July 2026) as the first dedicated economic assessment of geomagnetic storm impacts for the country, to inform mitigation decisions. It runs seven conservative disruption and mitigation scenarios for an extreme coronal mass ejection through a coupled physics-engineering-economic spatial modelling framework, focused on geomagnetically induced currents, and compares four ways to value power outages. Losses reach NZD 3.58 billion, 0.98 percent of annual GDP, in the worst unmitigated case; switching and islanding reach benefit-cost ratios up to 330 to 1 and GIC blocking devices up to 34.4 to 1. Coverage is national. Format and access: an open preprint with PDF. Licence: CC BY; free. Caveats: equipment losses and long-term revenue effects are not modelled, and the scenarios are first-order. It serves investment appraisal and resilience planning against space weather. Related catalogue records are the United States coupled modelling study by the same lead author and the WAPA neutral blocking device case.
